rationale: bugs_closed/285's DELIVERY half, found while closing that bug and measured today. The fence I shipped stops a page-scoped fix rewriting a SHARED TEMPLATE; it does not touch the second half of the same incident: the improver's delivery landed a section_edit (content_edit, field_updates {}) on an arbitrary ported page, the section editor re-rendered that slot, and webdesign.co.uk/learn/ai-builders/content-first.html served an EMPTY <article> plus three fabricated download links for ~23 hours. The per-slot floors are wired into exactly that write path (single_slot_floors.go, called from section_editor_actions.go's content_edit branch) and BOTH passed. Measured on the real archived pair (page_component_history ab400131… vs the poison row): the TEXT floor's axis is `<[^>]*>`-stripped length, which strips tags but not what is INSIDE <style>/<script>, so it read 3,245 → 8,492 chars = 262% retained; the CLASS floor read 3 → 4 attributes = 133%. Visible text (style/script/comment content excluded) fell 2,754 → 68 = 2%. Both axes GREW while the article was destroyed, so nothing on the path could refuse it. CALIBRATED ON EVERY ARCHIVED PAIR, not the motivating case: 117 overwrite pairs from migration 357's archive. The visible-text axis refuses exactly 1 — the poisoning write. The current tag-stripped axis also refuses exactly 1, and it is a DIFFERENT pair: putting the article back (2026-08-15 18:18Z, seed 431) reads 38% on that axis, i.e. the live floor would have REFUSED THE REPAIR had it gone through the editor. The axes disagree in both directions, which is why this is a correction of the axis and not an additional floor — and 'a guard that refuses good work gets switched off' is this estate's own recorded lesson (component_write_guard.go header). WHAT IT LOOSENS, measured and not waved at: evaluateSectionShrink applies its own minShrinkGuardChars (500) to the existing side, and applying that to VISIBLE text takes 31 of 117 pairs (26%) out of the text floor's scope — slots that are mostly CSS/JS. The old axis refused 0 of those 31, and on a CSS-dominated slot its ratio is dominated by the stylesheet, so it cannot see prose deletion there (this bug's whole finding); structural collapse on them is still covered by the unchanged class-attribute floor (bugs_open/253, own minimum of 10 classes). Of the 198 live rows this protects (9 sites, 118 pages: rows whose stored content cannot be reproduced from their content_data), 180 have ≥500 visible chars. SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY THE ONE PATH MY EVIDENCE COVERS. The whole-page save path (save_sections_shrink_guard.go) keeps the tag-stripped axis: its writes are DELETE+INSERT rebuilds, which the archive records as delete rows with no successor to pair against (3,603 of them against 281 overwrite rows), so there is no pair evidence for it. Changing an axis fleet-wide on evidence that does not cover it is how a guard starts refusing good work; that path's axis is filed as bugs_open/290 with the query. REUSE: no new floor, no new threshold, no new config key — the pure decision (evaluateSectionShrink), its 500-char minimum, the class floor, the refusal recorder (emitPruneRefusalWorkItem) and the step-config opt-outs are all unchanged and untouched. The change is which STRING is measured at one call site, plus one small helper. MUTATION-PROVEN, including one that exposed a defect in my own first draft: (MUT-1) revert the axis at the call site → TestEnforceSingleSlotFloors_RefusesTheStylesheetForProseSwap FAILS; (MUT-3) make visibleTextLength stop stripping <style> → 4 assertions fail; (MUT-2) delete the absolute minimum my first draft added → NOTHING failed, because minShrinkGuardChars=500 already dominates it, so that clause was dead code and is deleted rather than kept as decoration. My first four tests also all passed with the axis reverted (they exercised the arithmetic, not the wiring) — hence the enforcer-level test, which is the one that bites.

plan.summary: Correct the per-slot TEXT floor's measurement axis at the section-editor call site: measure VISIBLE text (style/script/comment content excluded) instead of tag-stripped length, so an edit that replaces a live article body with a stylesheet is refused and a repair of a hollowed slot is not. New helper file + a two-line change at one call site; no new floors, thresholds or config keys.
plan.risks: Loosening measured, not hypothetical: 31 of 117 archived pairs (26%) leave the text floor's scope because their existing side is under evaluateSectionShrink's own 500-char minimum once CSS/JS is excluded; the old axis refused 0 of those and is structurally blind to prose deletion on them, and the class-attribute floor still covers structural collapse there. Scope is the section-editor path only; the whole-page path is untouched because the archive cannot pair its DELETE+INSERT writes (filed as bugs_open/290). visibleTextLength is regex-based, not a parser: a <style> tag inside a string literal or an unclosed block degrades to counting that text, which is the pre-change behaviour and never stricter than it.

edits.rationale: The measurement, in its own file with the calibration table, the both-directions disagreement, the measured loosening and the scope limit — the evidence a future editor needs before changing it. Regex-based to match the package's existing stripper idiom; entities dropped rather than decoded because this is a quantity compared against another measured identically.

Feed the floor visible text instead of tag-stripped length, and say so in the refusal message so an operator knows which string was measured. The pure decision, the 500-char minimum, the class floor and the config opt-outs are unchanged.

Fixtures reproduce the real pair's shape and carry its measured ratios as assertions (2.62 on the old axis, 2% on the new), with guard assertions that fail if a fixture stops reproducing the trap — two of them fired during development and corrected my proportions. The enforcer-level test is what makes unwiring the axis fail the build.
